title: Rabbi Oshaya, Son of Rabbi Yehudah the Perfumer
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Chullin 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.55b.14) mentions him testifying before Rabbi Akiva, in Rabbi Tarfon’s name, that a flayed animal is unfit. [Tosefta Chullin 3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Chullin.3.3) instead names the witness Yehudah, son of Yeshayah the Perfumer. [Tosefta Sheviit, chapter 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Sheviit.5.8), likewise has Yehudah, son of Yeshayah the Perfumer, testifying before Rabbi Akiva in Rabbi Tarfon’s name that, in Hyman’s wording, the law of gleanings applies in the Sabbatical year.

notes.text: Geludah is an animal whose skin has been stripped away. The Bavli witness is Oshaya, son of Yehudah the Perfumer; the two Tosefta witnesses instead name Yehudah, son of Yeshayah the Perfumer.

Hyman cites Chullin 3:7. The linked Tosefta places the testimony at 3:3, with the same wording about the flayed animal. In the linked Sheviit, the Hebrew has לקטף, balsam, where Hyman has לקט, gleanings. The Hebrew says the Sabbatical year rule applies to balsam, while the accompanying English says it does not. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=270&lang=en) records the competing names of the witness.
